newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese retailer Jusco raided over scandal.
newsitem.headline: Japanese retailer Jusco raided over scandal.

text.p: Tokyo prosecutors raided the headquarters of major supermarket chain Jusco Co Ltd on Wednesday, a day after its president was arrested for previous links to a racketeer payoff scandal involving Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd.

A Jusco spokesman told Reuters that three officials from the prosecutors' office had entered Jusco's headquarters in Makuhari, in Chiba prefecture near Tokyo. He could not immediately confirm whether or not Jusco's other offices and branches were being raided.
"The prosecutors came to our Makuhari headquarters at 10.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) this morning and they are still here," the spokesman said, adding that he did not know the purpose of the raid.

On Tuesday, four former DKB executives including Kenji Tanaka, now president of Jusco, were arrested and half of the top Japanese commercial bank's 40 board members resigned in a shakeup which included the naming of a new president.
The affair has also ensnared Japan's biggest brokerage, Nomura Securities Co Ltd. There was no suggestion that Jusco itself was involved in the scandal.

Tokyo prosecutors said on Tuesday that they arrested the former DKB executives, who were responsible for screening the bank's loans for irregularities, on suspicion of making illicit loans to a "sokaiya" racketeer. Sokaiya extort money by threatening to disrupt shareholders meetings.
